docs.title: Welcome to MkDocs Demo
docs.text:
Live Demo

This site was built with MkDocs + Material theme and deployed automatically to GitHub Pages via GitHub Actions. Every git push to main triggers a new deployment — usually live in under 60 seconds.

docs.title: What is MkDocs?
docs.text: MkDocs is a fast, simple, and beautiful static site generator designed specifically for project documentation. Source files are written in Markdown and configured with a single YAML file.

docs.title: Why Material for MkDocs?
docs.text:
The Material theme is the most popular MkDocs theme. It gives you:

Feature Description :material-palette: Dark/Light mode Toggle between themes :material-magnify: Instant search Full-text search across all pages :material-navigation: Navigation tabs Clean top-level navigation :material-code-tags: Code highlighting Syntax highlighting with copy button :material-responsive: Responsive Looks great on mobile

docs.title: Key Features Shown in This Demo
docs.text:
NavigationSearchCode BlocksAdmonitions
  • Top-level tabs for major sections
  • Left sidebar for sub-pages
  • "Back to top" button
  • Click the search bar (or press /) and try searching for any term on this site
hello.py
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

print(greet("MkDocs"))

Pro Tip

Admonitions are a great way to highlight important information.

Watch Out

This is a warning block — useful for caveats and gotchas.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
This page demonstrates how to document an API in Markdown — a common use case for Docs as Code.

This is a demo

The endpoints below are illustrative examples showing how technical API docs look when written as Markdown and rendered by MkDocs.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
https://api.example.com/v2

All requests must include an Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <your-token>

docs.title: GET /users
docs.text:
Returns a paginated list of users.

Query Parameters

Parameter Type Required Description page integer No Page number (default: 1) per_page integer No Results per page (default: 20, max: 100) search string No Filter by name or email

Example Request

curl -X GET "https://api.example.com/v2/users?page=1&per_page=10" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..."

Example Response

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "usr_01HX2K",
      "name": "Ada Lovelace",
      "email": "ada@example.com",
      "created_at": "2024-01-15T09:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "page": 1,
    "per_page": 10,
    "total": 42
  }
}

docs.title: POST /users
docs.text:
Creates a new user.

Request Body

{
  "name": "Grace Hopper",
  "email": "grace@example.com",
  "role": "admin"
}

Response Codes

Code Meaning 201 Created User created successfully 400 Bad Request Missing or invalid fields 409 Conflict Email already exists

docs.title: DELETE /users/{id}
docs.text:
Irreversible

This action permanently deletes the user and all associated data. It cannot be undone.

Path Parameters

Parameter Type Description id string The user ID (e.g., usr_01HX2K)

Example Request

curl -X DELETE "https://api.example.com/v2/users/usr_01HX2K" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGci..."

docs.title: Error Format
docs.text:
All errors follow a consistent structure:

{
  "error": {
    "code": "VALIDATION_ERROR",
    "message": "The 'email' field is required.",
    "field": "email"
  }
}

docs.title: Documentation as Code
docs.text: Docs as Code means treating your documentation exactly the same way you treat your source code — written in plain text, stored in Git, reviewed in pull requests, and deployed automatically.

docs.title: The Core Idea
docs.text:
Traditional documentation lives in wikis, Word documents, or shared drives — isolated from the code it describes. Docs as Code brings documentation into the same version-controlled, peer-reviewed, CI/CD-driven workflow as your software.

Traditional Docs Docs as Code Word / Confluence / Wiki Markdown files in Git Manual copy/paste updates Auto-deployed on every git push No review process Pull Request review Version drift Always in sync with the codebase Silo'd from engineers Engineers write & own the docs

docs.title: The Three Pillars
docs.text:
1. Plain Text (Markdown)2. Version Control (Git)3. CI/CD (GitHub Actions)

Docs are written in Markdown — a simple, human-readable format that is:

  • Easy to learn (no special tools needed)
  • Diff-able in Git (git diff shows exactly what changed)
  • Portable across any documentation platform
  • Storable alongside source code in the same repo
# My Feature

This feature does X by calling Y.

!!! tip
    Use flag `--fast` for better performance.

Every documentation change is a commit. This means:

  • Full history of who changed what and why
  • Blame to find who wrote a particular paragraph
  • Branches for drafting new docs in parallel with development
  • Tags to snapshot docs for a specific release
  • Rollback any change instantly
# See who last changed a paragraph
git log -p docs/api-reference.md

# Create a docs branch alongside a feature branch
git checkout -b feature/new-api
# ... write code AND docs together ...
git push origin feature/new-api

Every merge to main triggers an automated pipeline that:

  1. Installs MkDocs dependencies
  2. Builds the static site
  3. Deploys to GitHub Pages

Zero manual steps. Zero stale documentation.

docs.title: Why It Matters
docs.text:
Docs stay in sync with code

When a developer changes an API, they update the doc in the same pull request. Reviewers catch outdated documentation before it ever ships.

Review docs like you review code

Pull Request comments, inline suggestions, and approval workflows apply to docs just as they do to code.

Anyone can contribute

Engineers, PMs, and technical writers all work in the same Markdown files with the same Git workflow they already know.

Always deployable

Because deployment is automated, the published site is always the latest version of main — never stale.

See the full workflow →

docs.title: The Docs as Code Workflow
docs.text: This page walks through the end-to-end lifecycle of a documentation change — from writing to publishing — using the same Git workflow used for code.

docs.title: The Full Lifecycle
docs.text:
graph TD
    A["📝 Write / Edit Markdown\n(any editor)"] --> B["git commit & push\n(feature branch)"]
    B --> C["Open Pull Request\non GitHub"]
    C --> D{"PR Review\n& Approval"}
    D -->|Changes requested| A
    D -->|Approved ✅| E["Merge to main"]
    E --> F["GitHub Actions triggers\nautomatically"]
    F --> G["mkdocs build\n(validates all links & syntax)"]
    G --> H["mkdocs gh-deploy\n(pushes to gh-pages branch)"]
    H --> I["🌐 Live on GitHub Pages\nhttps://12shubham.github.io/mkdocs-demo"]

docs.title: 1. Create a Branch
docs.text:
Always work on a feature branch — never commit docs directly to main.

git checkout -b docs/update-api-reference

docs.title: 2. Write in Markdown
docs.text:
Edit or create .md files in the docs/ folder. Use mkdocs serve to preview locally:

mkdocs serve
# Open http://127.0.0.1:8000 — hot-reloads on every save

Live Preview During Demo

Run mkdocs serve in a terminal, open the browser, then edit a .md file. The browser updates instantly — no manual refresh needed.

docs.title: 3. Commit and Push
docs.text:
git add docs/
git commit -m "docs: update API reference for v2 endpoints"
git push origin docs/update-api-reference

docs.title: 4. Open a Pull Request
docs.text:
Open a PR on GitHub. Your team can now:

  • Leave inline comments on specific lines of Markdown
  • Suggest edits directly in the GitHub UI
  • Approve or request changes — just like code review

Docs Review Checklist

  • [ ] Is the content accurate and up to date?
  • [ ] Are code examples correct and tested?
  • [ ] Are all internal links working?
  • [ ] Is the tone consistent with the rest of the docs?

docs.title: 5. Merge → Auto Deploy
docs.text:
Once the PR is approved and merged to main, GitHub Actions takes over:

.github/workflows/deploy.yml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main      # ← triggers on every merge to main

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt
      - run: mkdocs gh-deploy --force   # ← builds + deploys in one command

The site is live in under 60 seconds after merge.

docs.title: Folder Structure Convention
docs.text:
mkdocs-demo/
├── mkdocs.yml              ← Single config file for the entire site
├── requirements.txt        ← Pinned doc dependencies (reproducible builds)
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md            ← Home page
│   ├── docs-as-code/
│   │   ├── index.md        ← Concept overview
│   │   └── workflow.md     ← This page
│   ├── getting-started/
│   │   ├── installation.md
│   │   └── configuration.md
│   ├── api-reference.md
│   └── changelog.md
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── deploy.yml      ← CI/CD pipeline for auto-deploy

Convention: Docs Live Next to Code

Keep docs/ in the same repository as your source code. When a developer changes an API, updating the docs is part of the same PR — enforced by code review.

docs.title: Branching Strategy for Docs
docs.text:
Branch Pattern Purpose main Published docs (always deployed) docs/topic-name New doc page or section fix/typo-in-readme Quick corrections feature/new-feature Docs written alongside the feature code

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All MkDocs configuration lives in a single mkdocs.yml file at the root of your project.

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
mkdocs-demo/
├── mkdocs.yml          ← All configuration here
├── requirements.txt
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md        ← Home page
│   ├── getting-started/
│   │   ├── installation.md
│   │   └── configuration.md
│   ├── api-reference.md
│   └── changelog.md
└── .github/
    └── workflows/
        └── deploy.yml  ← Auto-deploy to GitHub Pages

docs.title: Site Metadata
docs.text:
site_name: My Project Docs
site_url: https://username.github.io/repo-name
site_description: A short description of your project
repo_url: https://github.com/username/repo-name

docs.title: Navigation
docs.text:
Define the left sidebar structure manually:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started:
    - Installation: getting-started/installation.md
    - Configuration: getting-started/configuration.md
  - API Reference: api-reference.md

Auto-navigation

If you omit nav:, MkDocs will auto-generate it from your file structure.

docs.title: Theme Options
docs.text:
theme:
  name: material
  palette:
    - scheme: default       # light mode
      primary: indigo
    - scheme: slate         # dark mode
      primary: indigo
  features:
    - navigation.tabs       # top-level tabs
    - navigation.top        # back-to-top button
    - search.suggest        # search autocomplete
    - content.code.copy     # copy button on code blocks

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
plugins:
  - search                  # built-in full-text search

docs.title: Markdown Extensions
docs.text:
markdown_extensions:
  - admonition              # !!! tip, !!! warning blocks
  - pymdownx.superfences    # code blocks inside admonitions
  - pymdownx.tabbed:        # === "Tab" syntax
      alternate_style: true
  - pymdownx.highlight:     # syntax highlighting
      anchor_linenums: true
  - tables                  # GitHub-flavored tables

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Get up and running with MkDocs and the Material theme in minutes.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.8+
  • pip package manager
  • git

Check your versions:

python --version   # Python 3.8+
pip --version
git --version

docs.title: Install Dependencies
docs.text:
pip (recommended)pip with requirements.txtconda 
pip install mkdocs-material

pip install -r requirements.txt

conda install -c conda-forge mkdocs-material

docs.title: Clone This Repo
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/12shubham/mkdocs-demo.git
cd mkdocs-demo
pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Run Locally
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000 in your browser. The site hot-reloads — edit any .md file and the browser refreshes instantly.

Live Edit During the Demo

Run mkdocs serve in one terminal, open the browser, then edit docs/index.md — your team will see changes appear instantly without refreshing.

docs.title: Deploy to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
git add .
git commit -m "my change"
git push origin main

GitHub Actions will automatically build and deploy to: https://12shubham.github.io/mkdocs-demo
